tagline.text: A 1,328 m dormant volcano in Ligao, Albay, facing Mayon head-on

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Amtic, Ligao City, Albay (Sitio Sabluyon trailhead)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,000~3,000 (per person, including shared guide fee, trailhead transport and registration; Manila round-trip transport not included)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Bicol International Airport (DRP, Daraga near Legazpi)

children.text: Mount Masaraga is a dormant volcano of about 1,328 m in Ligao City, Albay, and the peak closest to Mayon Volcano. After a steep climb up a cogon-grass ridge, the summit rewards you with views of Mayon and Mount Isarog on a clear day, but it is a demanding hike that requires a guide.
Mount Masaraga is a stratovolcano rising about

above sea level in Ligao City, Albay Province, in the Bicol region of southeastern Luzon. Wikipedia describes it as a forested, sharp-topped mountain, and the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (PHIVOLCS) classifies it as inactive. No historical eruptions are known (the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program lists it with no recorded eruptions); it is built mainly of andesite as part of the Bicol Volcanic Chain, and thick Holocene lava flows lie on its flanks. The name may be unfamiliar, but locally it is grouped with Mayon Volcano and Mount Malinao as the "Magayon Trio."

The main reason to climb it is its location. Masaraga is the peak closest to Mayon's cone, so from the summit you get a rare, long side-on view of Mayon. In good weather the panorama stretches 360 degrees to the Sabluyon road, Mount Malinao and Mount Isarog. Unlike the usual Legazpi view looking up at Mayon, hikers come here at dawn to face the volcano at eye level. The commonly quoted height is 1,328 m, while some blogs give about 1,350 m, so there is no need to fixate on one number.

The hike is not easy. The Philippine mountaineering community Pinoy Mountaineer rates it 6 out of 9, a "major climb," with trail class 1–4. It starts on concrete road and through coconut and abaca farms, but from the midsection a sun-exposed cogon-grass ridge takes over, with stretches where you must pull yourself up by grabbing the grass. Reports put the time to the summit at about
3 hours
at the fastest and usually
4–7 hours
. When it rains the soil becomes slippery and far more dangerous, so it is not recommended for beginners or for the rainy season.
The trailhead is Sitio Sabluyon in Barangay Amtic, Ligao City. It is within about an hour by car from Legazpi, and about
25 minutes

by motorbike from central Ligao. The trail straddles the boundary of Ligao and Tabaco, so some people approach from the Tabaco side. Unlike a typical day hike in Korea, a pre-dawn start is the norm, and registration and guide arrangements must be made in advance, so preparation matters as much as the climb. A few practical words for first-timers: Masaraga is not a park with tourist facilities but a simple hiking destination led by villagers. Do not expect signboards, restaurants or shops, and confirm the time, fee and meeting place with your guide by text message beforehand. Guide fees are often charged per group even for small parties, so gathering companions at a Legazpi guesthouse or through hiking communities and splitting the cost eases the burden. If you are worried about your fitness, warm up on a lower Bicol hill such as the Quitinday hills before taking this on.

The greatest reward at the Masaraga summit is Mayon Volcano. Because this is the peak nearest to Mayon, you can see its smooth cone from the side at length, and on a clear dawn it rises above the clouds. Clouds soon cover it as they climb, so arriving before sunrise is best.

Beyond the midpoint the route follows a steep cogon-grass ridge. There are deep ravines on both sides and the soft soil makes your feet sink. You will often grab the grass to climb, so gloves are essential. This section sets the difficulty of the whole hike.

The start passes along a paved road, coconut and abaca farms and an open clearing, followed by patches of forest. The scenery changes with altitude, so it never gets dull. Hikers mention huts (kubo) for resting and a campsite along the way.
The summit is described as nearly flat grassland. In good weather you can see Mayon, the Sabluyon road, Mount Malinao and Mount Isarog. Strong winds are common, so bring a thin windproof jacket.

blocks.title: The story of the Magayon Trio

children.text: Mayon, Masaraga and Malinao are together called the "Magayon Trio." Because climbing to Mayon's summit is restricted, Masaraga is often mentioned as the alternative for anyone who wants a real mountain hike in Bicol.

blocks.title: Albay sights to add before or after

children.text: A popular plan is to visit Quitinday Green Hills, Sumlang Lake, Cagsawa Ruins and Daraga Church the day before or after the hike. It is fun to compare the same Mayon seen from low ground with the view from the summit.

items.title: Pre-dawn sunrise day hike
items.subtitle: Stay in Ligao, then watch sunrise from the summit

children.text: Wake up at your lodging in Ligao (or Tabaco), eat lightly and pack water. Arrange the ride to the trailhead the day before.
Arrive at the Amtic trailhead, register, and set off with your guide by headlamp. The early part passes paved road and farm tracks.
The rest-hut and campsite section. The steep ridge begins from here. Eat and drink plenty of food and water now.
Reach the summit for sunrise and the Mayon view. Reported climbing times range from about 3 to 7 hours, so treat this timing as the fastest case.
Start down before the clouds rise. The descent is slippery, so slow down.
Back at the trailhead, wash up and have lunch at the guide's house or in the village.
Trip reports differ a lot on timing. If your fitness is average, add
1–2 hours
of margin to the times above.

items.title: Daytime hike and Albay tour
items.subtitle: A two-day plan that also sees Mayon from lower ground

children.text: From Legazpi, visit Cagsawa Ruins and Daraga Church and look up at Mayon from below.
Take a light stroll around Quitinday Green Hills or Sumlang Lake, then move to your Ligao lodging and sleep early.
Climb Masaraga and come down in the morning.
Return from Ligao to Legazpi, have lunch, and take a bus or flight to Manila.
A flight from Manila toward Legazpi takes about
1 hour
. Bicol International Airport (DRP) opened in Daraga in October 2021 and Manila flights are operated by Cebu Pacific and PAL Express, so check the airline and airport details beforehand.
A bus from Manila to Legazpi costs about
(2026 published bus fares, possibly higher with fuel surcharges), and an overnight bus gets you there in the morning.
The bus passes through Ligao, so you can ask the conductor to let you off at Sabluyon Junction.
Bus fares and schedules change, so check the latest information.
Take a jeepney from the terminals near Legazpi market, or a van from the central terminal near Gaisano Mall. The fare was about
in a 2011 report and may be higher now, so confirm locally. Vehicles leave when full.
It takes about
1 hour
to Ligao.
From Ligao, take a jeepney toward Tabaco and ask to be dropped at Sitio Sabluyon. From central Ligao it is about
25 minutes
by motorbike to the trailhead.
There are no jeepneys at dawn, so guides often arrange a motorbike taxi (habal-habal). Trip reports from 2014~2017 mention about
per person, so settle the fare before you set off.
The first public jeepney usually leaves around
. For a pre-dawn start, arrange transport in advance.

Most of the ridge is open grassland without shade, so the weather decides the hike. On rainy days the soil is slippery, and low cloud can hide Mayon. In the dry season the trail is firmer and leeches are fewer, so the dry season is recommended.

Within a day, a pre-dawn start is best. A clear sky around sunrise favors the Mayon view, and you avoid the hot midday sun. Check the forecast before leaving, and if clouds are heavy, postponing by a day is an option.

Most people stay in Ligao or Tabaco the night before. Trip reports mention JJ Midcity Inn and Tabaco Gardenia Hotel in Tabaco, a bed and breakfast in Ligao, and a spring resort in Buang, the closest to the trailhead. Prices and operating status change, so confirm before booking. Staying in Legazpi and hiring a car at dawn is possible but inconvenient.
There are no restaurants or water sources on the mountain, so carry at least
2 liters or more

of water per person and plenty of snacks. After the hike, try Bicol cuisine in downtown Ligao or Legazpi, such as Bicol Express and laing. Dishes with coconut milk and chili are a feature of the region.

After the hike, a place where you can shower and do laundry is welcome. Sweat, soil and leech marks will make your clothes very dirty, so pack a change of clothes and plastic bags, and ask your lodging in advance for a check-out time later than your expected return. If you take an overnight bus to Manila, plan to wash up and rest near the Legazpi terminal after descending.

A guide is close to mandatory. Register at the village (Amtic) and city hall, climb with a local guide, and confirm contact numbers with your lodging or city hall since published numbers may be out of date.
Wear long sleeves and long pants with gloves. Cogon grass is sharp and will cut bare hands.
Bring trekking shoes and poles; a headlamp and power bank are essential for a pre-dawn hike.
There is no water source up to the summit, so bring plenty. Sun protection and sunscreen are also needed.
In leech season, bring salt-water spray or leech socks.
For a pre-dawn hike, sleep early the night before and save your strength. Lodging in Ligao or Tabaco, near the trailhead, is best.
Keep your pack light, and store a rain jacket and a change of clothes separately in plastic bags.
Mobile signal is weak in places, so download an offline map.
Masaraga's ridge is slippery and dangerous in the rain. Beginners should never climb alone and must go with a local guide.
Danger zones around Mayon Volcano are defined, so check volcanic activity alerts from the Albay disaster authorities first.
The ridge has almost no shade, so watch for heatstroke and dehydration, and turn back immediately if you suspect them.
The ridge has deep ravines, so do not leave the path and follow your guide's instructions.
In the rainy season, leeches and fast-changing weather are hazards, and fog makes it easy to lose the trail.
Fees, registration methods and access rules change from year to year, so check the latest with Ligao city hall or the Amtic barangay hall before you go.
It is the subject best seen from Masaraga. Look up at it from low ground the day before and compare its side profile from Masaraga the next day.
It is within about
30 minutes
by car from Legazpi and famous for photos with Mayon in the background.
An old church on a hill with a view of Mayon, good to visit before or after the Masaraga hike.
The Masaraga trail straddles the Ligao–Tabaco boundary, so Tabaco is used as a base for lodging.
The central city of Bicol, with the airport, bus terminals and lodging, a good starting point.
